<assessment>SOURCE is one street-level oblique view: a tall right tower steps down toward a connected low wing and left block. Visible features include a pale projecting grid, recessed glazing and selected outdoor bays, planted setbacks, flat roof edges and a darker lower facade zone. CURRENT 10–12 retain this overall arrangement, the corrected six-front/five-side tower subdivisions and several clearly recessed loggias. The principal remaining mismatch is the distribution of open versus glazed tower cells, especially the missing planted corner pocket above the dark facade band. CURRENT 11 supports retaining the corrected low-wing terrace pockets. Rear elevations and concealed joints cannot be verified against this single source view; the captures do not establish slab penetration or floating railings. SOURCE includes a separate neighbor and street context, but their recorded removal intent conflicts with earlier retention requirements; the invalid host scope does not settle that conflict, so restoration is not requested.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: SOURCE shows a distinctive planted, recessed corner-adjacent pocket above the dark lower facade zone and an irregular arrangement of open cells. CURRENT 10 and 12 retain glazing at that landmark and distribute several recesses differently, leaving the tower more uniformly enclosed.
action: Locally correct the source-identifiable infill and recess positions, including the planted corner pocket, within the existing grid. Retain corrected bay divisions, floor elevations and completed deep loggias. Connect each corrected recess floor, side returns, soffit and railing; keep planting clear of enclosure and guards. Do not assign exact depths or hidden construction from this image.</issue>
<keep>Corrected six-front/five-side tower bay subdivisions.
Pale projecting tower grid members and aligned floor divisions.
Completed deep loggia side returns and soffits visible in CURRENT 12.
Recessed planted low-wing terrace pockets visible in CURRENT 11.</keep>
